verdict.rationale: Kong documents its own authentication and authorization for APIs (JWT, basic auth, OAuth, ACLs), so it can issue credentials and restrict access by ACL. Its Dev Portal lets developers manage their own credentials, and Konnect claims agent-level entitlements down to MCP tools. However, nothing documents how a scoped, least-privilege credential is actually issued to an agent, or how those scopes are defined. missing for 10: documented per-agent credential issuance workflow, explicit scope/permission granularity for agent credentials, scoped Konnect/Admin API tokens for agents, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Authentication and authorization for APIs using methods like JWT, basic auth, OAuth, ACLs and more.
Define entitlements, meter, and bill against agent context consumption for everything from the agent to the LLM to the MCP server to MCP tools.
